analysis: The PR changes only documentation (docs/operations/provider-release.md lines 311-320) and a release-pipeline test (scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py, around line 180). No runtime provider code, trust boundary, key, attestation or authorization logic is touched. The doc change says `qualify-sdk` sets `DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT: prod`, so SDK tests see production defaults on every branch, and that on `dev` an unset value compiles the dev identity. The test change is stricter than before: it asserts that qualify-sdk does not use the resolve-env selector and that its only DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT assignment is the literal `prod`. That keeps the qualification job from inheriting the dev/staging environment, which is the safer direction. The release signing, staging and registration flow is unchanged, so T-034, T-054, T-061 and the TB-011 build qualification contract are not weakened. The rest of the doc (v0.10.4 preparation notes, rollout order, dev/staging identity, dev-branch lane) was read. It describes the unchanged process, and my diff-based review found no new attack surface. Open points for integration: (1) I did not see the workflow YAML, so I could not confirm that qualify-sdk actually sets `prod`; the test only asserts that. (2) The doc already notes that review is not enforced on the `dev` branch while it gets the Developer ID signature. That is a preexisting stated gap, not a regression from this PR, and it needs a repository-admin rule outside the supplied evidence. (3) I could not verify the Package.swift behavior the doc describes for an unset value.
